In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Kawthar

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾.

Al-Kawthar is on the pattern fawʿal, derived from al-kathrah (abundance). The verb aʿtaynākа (We have granted you) was also read as anṭaynāka, with the ʿayn replaced by a nūn. The nūn is not a substitution for the ʿayn, as the replacement of the alif for a waw or a ʿayn in hollow verbs and the like is; rather, each of the two is a root in its own right and a separate reading. So said Abū Ḥayyān.

Scholars differ concerning al-Kawthar.

It is said to be a proper noun (ʿalam).

It is said to be a descriptive term (waṣf).

Those who hold it to be a proper noun say that it is the name of a river in Paradise. Those who hold it to be a descriptive term say that it means abundant good.

Among what is cited as evidence for its being a proper noun is what came in the sound ḥadīths in the Sunnah, which Ibn Kathīr and others have mentioned.

In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, on the authority of Anas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken up to the heaven, he said: 'I came to a river whose banks were domes of pearls, hollow. I said: What is this, O Jibrīl? He said: This is al-Kawthar.'"

And with the same chain, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, "she was asked about His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and she said: It is a river given to your Prophet ﷺ, whose two banks are of hollow pearls, and whose vessels are as numerous as the stars."

And with the same chain, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said concerning al-Kawthar: It is the good which Allah gave him.

Abū Bishr said: I said to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: People claim that it is a river in Paradise. Saʿīd said: The river in Paradise is of the good which Allah gave him.

Ibn Kathīr mentioned these ḥadīths and others on the authority of Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on him. Among them, by Aḥmad's chain to (p-127) Anas ibn Mālik, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dozed off, then raised his head smiling. Either he said it to them, or they said to him: Why are you laughing? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: A surah has just been revealed to me, and he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, until he finished it. Then he said: Do you know what al-Kawthar is? They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: It is a river my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, granted me in Paradise, upon which is abundant good. My ummah will come to it on the Day of Resurrection; its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant will be pulled away from it, and I will say: My Lord, he is of my ummah. It will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you."

Ibn Kathīr also mentioned what came concerning the description of the Basin (ḥawḍ). These texts indicate that al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise which Allah gave to His Messenger ﷺ.

In the last ḥadīth from Imam Aḥmad, his saying "upon which is abundant good" suggests that the meaning of description is present.

For this reason some exegetes said: It is abundant good.

Among those who said so is Ibn ʿAbbās, as already mentioned in the ḥadīth of al-Bukhārī from him.

They cited for this meaning the verse of the poet al-Kumayt:

"You are abundant, O son of Marwān, good, and your father was the son of the excellent lineages."

What the soul finds reassuring is that al-Kawthar is abundant good, and that the Basin or the river is part of that.

Verses have also come indicating that Allah granted His Messenger abundant good, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the great Qur'an﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 87].

Nearby is Surah al-Ḍuḥā, in which: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 5], followed by great blessings: the expansion of the breast, the removal of the burden, the raising of your mention, and ease after hardship.

After it, in Surah al-Tīn, He made His city (al-balad al-amīn) and gave the believers who do righteous deeds a reward never to be cut off.

After it, Surah "Iqra'" (al-ʿAlaq): He bestowed upon him the Qur'an and taught him what he did not know.

Then Surah al-Qadr: He gave him a night better than a thousand months.

Then Surah al-Bayyinah: He made his ummah the best of creation, granted them His pleasure, and made them pleased with Him.

Then Surah al-Zalzalah: He preserved their deeds for them, so He did not waste for them even the weight of an atom of good.

In Surah al-ʿĀdiyāt: the greatest deed is jihad, so He swore by the charging steeds in the way of Allah and the victory over the enemies.

In Surah al-Takāthur: their nurture upon His blessings, so that they would be thankful for them, and He would increase them of His bounty.

In Surah al-ʿAṣr: He made his ummah the best ummah brought forth for mankind, who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds, enjoin one another to the truth and call to it, and enjoin one another to patience and are steadfast upon it.

After it, in Surah Quraysh: Allah honoured his people, secured them, and gave them the two journeys.

In the surah immediately before it, Surah al-Māʿūn: a complete comparison can be made, first.

In general, if the hypocrites withhold al-māʿūn, then We have given you abundant good, second.

In detail, in the first: He described the hypocrites and the deniers by repelling the orphan, while in al-Ḍuḥā He had clarified to him the right of the orphan: ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 9]. So he was the best guardian and the best caretaker, and He described them here as not urging the feeding of the needy.

He also clarified to him in al-Ḍuḥā: ﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel him﴾, so he used to prefer the petitioner over himself, whereas these are heedless of their prayer, showing off with their deeds.

In this surah: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ [al-Kawthar: 2], the performance of prayer sincerely for their Lord, and feeding the needy by slaughtering the sacrificial animal, the offering and charity. All of that is abundant good, to which is added what the Sunnah has brought, as in the ḥadīth: "I have been given five things that none before me was given: I was made victorious through terror over a distance of a month's journey; intercession was given to me; spoils were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; a prophet used to be sent only to his own people, but I was sent to all mankind; and the earth was made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whoever the prayer reaches let him pray."

(p-129) And his saying: "My ummah's error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do has been lifted from me."

And in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not impose upon us that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286].

He ﷺ said: "Allah, may He be exalted, said: I have done it, I have done it."

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 79], which is the station for which the first and the last will envy him.

Beyond these texts, which confirm the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, in al-Bukhārī: that al-Kawthar is abundant good, and that the river in Paradise is from this al-Kawthar which was given to him ﷺ.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.﴾

In this verse, together with what precedes it, there is a link between blessings and giving thanks for them, and between acts of worship and what they require. Just as He gave you al-Kawthar, so let him pray to his Lord, glorified is He, and sacrifice to Him. This is as has already been mentioned in Surat Quraysh, in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ [Quraysh: 3-4].

Here, ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾, which is greater than their journey (in winter and summer) and their security, and ﴿so pray to your Lord﴾ corresponds to ﴿so let them worship the Lord of this House﴾.

It has also been said: since the preceding surah explained the condition of the hypocrites, who are heedless of the prayer and show off in their deeds, this surah brings the good example: ﴿so pray to your Lord﴾, sincere to Him in your worship, as has been mentioned in the surah before it: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110].

As for His words, Exalted is He, addressing the Prophet himself (ﷺ) in teaching the Ummah: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds would surely be lost﴾ [al-Zumar: 65], despite his (ﷺ) being protected from anything less than that. The prayer is general, and the obligatory prayer is what is especially meant.

(p-130) It has also been said that the prayer is the Eid prayer, and as for the sacrifice (nahr), several views have been stated about it:

The first: it refers to the sacrificing of the hady (offering) or the sacrificing of the udhiyah (sacrificial animal). This is linked to the view of those who understood the prayer as the Eid prayer, and that the sacrifice comes after the prayer, as in the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: "He sacrificed before praying, and he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) urging the udhiyah after the prayer, so he said: 'Indeed, I knew today is a day of meat, so I hastened with my sacrifice.' He (ﷺ) said to him: 'Is your sheep a sheep for meat?' He said: 'Indeed, we have a young female goat which is dearer to us than a sheep. Will it suffice for me?' He said: 'Sacrifice it, but it will not suffice for anyone other than you.'"

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already given a full discussion of the udhiyah at His words: ﴿So eat from it and feed the miserable, the poor﴾ [al-Hajj: 28]. Some have said, regarding the meaning of "wanhar": i.e., place your right hand upon your left on your chest (nahr) during the prayer, and this is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Other views are also stated for which there is no explicit text.

The nahr is the stabbing of the camel at the lower part of the neck, at the place of sacrifice where the neck meets the chest.

The most correct view regarding the prayer and the sacrifice is what has preceded: the generality of the prayer and the generality of the nahr or dhabh (slaughter), because of what came in His words: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am: 162].

The jurists agree that the nahr is for camels and the dhabh is for sheep and goats, while cattle are disputed between nahr and dhabh. They unanimously agree that this is the preferred practice. Were one to use nahr for all animals, or dhabh for all animals, it would be permissible, but it would be contrary to the Sunnah.

They said: the wisdom in specifying the camel for nahr is its long neck. Had it been slaughtered (dhabh), the path of the blood from the heart to the place of slaughter would be long, so it would not easily help the release of all the blood. By contrast, nahr at the place of sacrifice shortens the distance and helps the heart to push out all the blood. As for sheep, dhabh is suitable for them. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 108, verse 3:**

(p-131) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Surely the one who hates you is the one cut off [from good]﴾ [108:3]. Al-Bukhari said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Sha'innaka" means "your enemy." (end of quotation)

Al-Abtar is the one who is cut off, the one who has no offspring.

Abu Hayyan cited the verse of the poet:

*A base man, on whose nose the khunzuwana (a mark of arrogance) has appeared, cutting off the near kin; cutting, the ones who are cut off.*

He also said: "Sha'innaka" means "the one who hates you."

In this verse, Allah, glorified and exalted, informs us that the one who hates the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the one cut off.

It was said that it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il. He said to the Quraysh: "Leave him, for he is abtar (cut off), with no offspring. When he dies, you will be at ease." So Allah, exalted, revealed this as a rebuttal on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Its fulfilment in action came in the battle of Badr, in His saying: ﴿And Allah intends to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers﴾ [8:7]. He killed the chieftains of the Quraysh, and fulfilled the warning concerning them.

Similar to this is the general meaning of His saying: ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [6:45].

And there is: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [111:1].

So it has the same meaning as well.

The remembrance of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remains in his offspring from among the people of his household, and in his entire community, as has already been mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾ [94:4].
